title: Hand the tenant to work on another thread

blocks.text: This practice continues the billing service's `TenantContext`: its `runAs(...)` is the one you wrote, already in place.

Billing jobs now send notifications on a separate notifier pool, so that a slow mail server doesn't hold up an invoice run. The notification code reads `TenantContext.current()` to pick the tenant's sender address and template. The first attempt sent notifications with no tenant at all; a quick fix made every notification go out under the name of one tenant, the one whose job happened to run first after the deploy.

Write `wrap(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/TenantContext.java`. A job calls it on a task before handing the task to another thread. When you're done, a wrapped task runs as the tenant of the job that wrapped it, on any thread and whichever job started that thread, and leaves the thread as it found it. About five lines in total.
The tests run each job on a thread of its own and send its notification through a one-thread pool that the first job to use it starts.

cases.says: a wrapped task run on the job's own thread runs as the job's tenant
a wrapped task run on a pool thread runs as the tenant of the job that wrapped it
a pool thread first started during one tenant's job runs a later tenant's task as that later tenant
after a wrapped task, a plain task on the same pool thread sees no tenant

origin.section: InheritableThreadLocal Copies the Value Once, When a Thread Is Created

concepts: InheritableThreadLocal copies values once, when a thread is created, so a pool's threads keep what their creator had; a value for a task is captured at submit time and set in the task.
